answer:
**答案（自然语言假设）**：该变量是 **SES（家庭社会经济地位）**。当基线模型只包含 SES 与种族（及性别）背景变量时，SES 对 BA 学位完成的效应为正且高度显著（logit 系数约 +0.35～+0.36，p<0.001，OR≈1.43）；一旦同时纳入学业特征（ASVAB 综合分数与班级百分位），SES 的系数翻转为负（约 −0.23，OR≈0.79）并失去显著性（p 从 <0.001 升至约 0.02–0.07，在 1% 水平上不再显著；在含家庭规模的线性概率模型中 p=0.66，完全不显著）。机制解释：SES 的表观正效应绝大部分是由其与学业能力的关联中介的（corr(SES, ASVAB)=0.46，corr(SES, 班级百分位)=0.30）——在学业成绩相同的条件下，家庭社会经济地位较高者并不更可能完成 BA 学位（条件效应甚至略为负向）；换言之，观察到的 SES 优势实际上反映的是学业资源配置（测试成绩与班级排名）的差异，而非 SES 本身的独立因果效应。种族系数呈现相反的变化（Black 从 −0.30 变为 +0.52 并转为显著），进一步说明学业变量吸收的正是背景差异中与成绩相关的部分。

**其他变量的核查**（全部候选变量中唯有 SES 符合"0.3636→−0.2293 + 失去显著性"模式）：性别（−0.25→−0.27，始终不显著）、家庭规模（−0.61→−0.52，始终显著为负）、race_Black（符号翻转但变为显著）、race_Hispanic（−0.07→+0.29，始终不显著且 M1 系数与目标不符）。

**复现网格要点**（9 种设定 × 稳健/经典标准误，见 final_grid.csv）：
- logit、SES 原始量纲、基线含种族(+性别)、**不含家庭规模**：+0.3548 (se 0.088, p<0.001) → −0.2379 (se 0.101, p=0.018)；不含性别时 +0.3524 → −0.2316 (p=0.021)；cloglog 链接给出 −0.2290，与目标 −0.2293 几乎一致。
- **家庭规模是符号翻转的关键调节变量**：logit 中若 M2 同时含家庭规模，SES 保持正值 (+0.2906)；LPM 中若含家庭规模则 SES 翻转为 −0.0013 且完全不显著 (p=0.66)。
- 班级百分位编码方向只影响其自身系数符号（+0.0203 vs −0.0203），不影响 SES 系数；数据特征（高 ASVAB 者百分位≈97.8）表明高分=排名更好。
- 稀有事件诊断：M2 logit 收敛正常、预测概率 0.0003–0.47、无分离；VIF 均 <2.7（ASVAB 与百分位相关 0.70 但未达病态程度）。

**不确定之处（如实说明）**：精确复现 0.3636/−0.2293 未完全达成——最接近的 logit 设定给出 0.3548/−0.2379，cloglog 给出 −0.2290；差异可能源于原分析未公开的样本裁剪或实现细节。且在最接近的设定下 M2 的 p≈0.018–0.038（1% 水平不显著，5% 水平边缘显著）；"失去显著性"在 1% 阈值及 LPM（含家庭规模，p=0.66）下成立。变量识别（SES）在所有测过的 27 种设定组合中均稳健。

payload.hypothesis: SES (socioeconomic status) is the variable whose effect on BA degree completion decreases from ~0.3636 to ~-0.2293 and loses significance when race and academic characteristics (ASVAB composite score and class percentile) are added. In nested logistic regressions on n=8,773 (BA completion rate 2.7%), the SES log-odds coefficient falls from +0.3548 (se=0.088, p<0.001, OR=1.43; race-only base: +0.3524; cloglog: +0.3471) to -0.2379 (se=0.101, p=0.018, OR=0.79; cloglog: -0.2290 ≈ target -0.2293) once academic measures enter; it is insignificant at the 1% level (robust-SE p≈0.033), and in the linear probability model with family size included it flips to -0.0013 and is clearly insignificant (p=0.66). The apparent positive SES gradient is mediated by academic resources: SES correlates 0.46 with the ASVAB composite and 0.30 with class percentile, and conditional on measured academic performance, higher-SES students are no more (if anything slightly less) likely to complete a BA. Including family size reverses the flip (SES stays +0.29), so family size is a key suppressor; no other variable (sex, family size, race dummies) matches the 0.3636→-0.2293 sign-flip-and-loss-of-significance pattern across any tested specification.
payload.workflow: 1) Data audit: 8,773 rows x 8 cols, zero missing; BA=236 events (2.7%); race 3-category; SES standardized; verified no duplicate CASE IDs. 2) Nested models: logit with base (SES+sex+race dummies, White ref) vs full (+ASVAB composite + class percentile), plus average marginal effects; LPM (HC1) as robustness. 3) Systematic replication grid: {logit, probit, cloglog, LPM} x covariate sets (race/sex/family size in/out) x SES raw/standardized x percentile raw/reversed x classical/HC0-HC3 SEs, searching for the 0.3636→-0.2293 path (best match: logit, raw SES, family size excluded; 27 specifications stored in CSV). 4) Diagnostics: ASVAB-percentile correlation 0.70 but all VIFs <2.7; M2 logit converged with no separation (fitted probabilities 0.0003-0.47); flip scan of every candidate variable; percentile-coding sensitivity check (reversal flips only the percentile's own coefficient, leaving SES unchanged).
